newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Food sees substantial U.S. H2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Food sees substantial U.S. H2 loss.

text.p: Yorkshire Food Group Plc said on Wednesday that it expected to make a "substantial" loss at its U.S. operations in the second half of the year due to the termination of its U.S. distribution agreement and a poor raisin crop.
The company said in a statement that it would not pay a dividend for the full year. It also announced the resignation of David Morgan as finance director.

"The difficulties in the U.S. operations and fluctuations in crop rices, particularly for almonds, will further result in costs and loss of margin totalling some six million stg," Yorkshire Foods said.
The announcement hit the group's share price, which had plunged 12-1/2 pence to 32 pence by 1608 GMT, recovering from a low of 25 pence.
Yorkshire Foods made a pre-tax loss of 4.1 million stg in the first six months of the year, but indicated in September that it expected its U.S. operations to be profitable in the second half.
Yorkshire said the decision of its U.S. sales and distribution agent to terminate its agreement with effect from June 1997 had already hit sales of its Del Monte brand products.
In light of the expected losses, Yorkshire said it was in "constructive discussions" with its bankers "about the level of continuing support required".
The group, which specialises in the processing, packaging and distribution of foodstuffs, said it still expected its UK operations to "produce no significant loss in the second half".
Yorkshire said chief executive Paul Haley would replace David Morgan as financial director. Haley was financial director until March 1995.
Michael Firth is to resume the posts of chairman and chief executive with immediate effect, the company added.
